EcoPark 3D Sorting Game

Thoughts

Designing Educational Game

I'm focusing on creating a web game for 7-10 year olds. It needs to be interactive, bright, and have a 3D aesthetic, all in a single HTML file. The goal is easy deployment on any website, leveraging HTML5, CSS3, and Three.js through either a CDN or WebGL/Three.js directly.

Refining Open World

I'm now zeroing in on an open-world design, envisioning a cozy pastel park built in Three.js. Players will navigate via clicks, keys, or a virtual joystick. The core mechanic will be dragging and dropping trash into bins, making sure this is very intuitive on both mouse and touch interfaces, utilizing Pointer Events for broad device compatibility. I'm focusing on ensuring it works on any website, via iframe or standalone.

Optimizing Dragging Mechanics

I'm now iterating on the trash-collecting mechanic in my 3D open world. To enhance player experience, I'm integrating several design features: 3D recycling stations placed throughout the park and glowing trash item clusters with bobbing animation and a "Find Next Trash" helper button or mini-compass. This should make dragging and dropping trash into bins feel more intuitive. The park will have a sunny, pastel low-poly aesthetic.

Implementing Bin Interaction

I'm working on the trash-collecting mechanic's user interface. I'm prioritizing user-friendliness with either camera framing of the trash item or a bottom-screen "Bin Bar" with 3D icons. Alternatively, users will drag and drop items directly onto visible 3D bins in the scene. I am now exploring an always-visible, "chunky" bin-dock system for broad accessibility.

Refining Game Palette

I am now focusing on the visual style for the game. I am aiming for a soft pastel color scheme to be appealing to the target age group of 7-10 years old. I'm considering sky blue, minty grass, and cream paths, along with coral/peach, lavender, and sunny yellow. I am also exploring a rounded, clay-like, 3D UI card design (claymorphism) for a friendly aesthetic.

Expanding Trash Categories

I'm expanding the trash categories, including both organic and anorganic items for recycling education, specifically plastic and metal. I'm focusing on large, finger-friendly button sizes and rounded, tactile designs with bottom borders. I'm prioritizing user experience with a rounded typeface and large hitboxes. I'm working to make the trash items big, and the raycast spheres on 3D objects are forgiving so children don't miss.

Categorizing Trash Items

I'm now expanding trash categories to provide variety and educational value. I've added plastic, glass, and metal items, also paper and cardboard items, and a red bin for hazardous waste. I want to build these in Three.js for simplicity and to avoid external dependencies. Immediate, positive feedback and educational popups are also a priority.

Adding Educational Explanations

I'm now incorporating educational explanations for correct and incorrect trash placements, creating an interactive learning experience. Incorrect placements will trigger gentle feedback and corrective popups. I'm also planning a "Trash Encyclopedia" and progress tracking. A celebration screen with a "Play Again" button will appear upon completion.

Enhancing Drag Feedback

I've made progress on the trash-collecting mechanic's feedback system. A floating badge or icon now follows the finger/cursor when a trash item is dragged. I'm prioritizing accuracy and comfort for children. I'm now making bins scale up, glow, and open their lids when the finger hovers over them, giving immediate tactile feedback.

Developing World Controls

I'm now focusing on player movement and world interaction. There's a 3D pastel character, and I'm implementing tap-to-walk, WASD/arrow keys, and an on-screen D-pad. Easy camera zoom/rotate buttons are also planned. I'm prioritizing direct trash item clicking and a compass-style "Guide Me" button.

Here is a complete, single-file 3D Interactive Open-World Trash Sorting Game ("EcoPark 3D").

Because it is built in a single self-contained HTML file using Three.js and Web Audio, you can open it directly in any browser, host it on any website, or embed it inside an <iframe> on WordPress, Wix, or any educational platform.

Key Features Included:

  • Bright, Soft-Pastel 3D Open World: A sunny park with trees, a pond, flower patches, park benches, clouds, and a cute 3D character you can walk around (using tap-to-walk, arrow keys/WASD, or on-screen camera buttons).

  • Comfortable Finger-Friendly Drag & Drop: Large hitboxes on all 3D trash items, smooth touch/mouse dragging (pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup with touch-action: none), and big, squishy 3D-style bin buttons at the bottom that pop up and open when you drag near them.

  • 4 Trash Categories & 14 Unique 3D Items:

    • Organic (Green): Banana Peel, Apple Core, Watermelon Rind, Fallen Leaves

    • Anorganic / Recyclables (Blue): Plastic Bottle, Soda Can, Glass Jar, Plastic Cup

    • Paper & Cardboard (Amber): Cardboard Box, Newspaper, Paper Bag

    • Hazardous / B3 (Coral/Red): Used Battery, Broken Lightbulb, Old Paint Can

  • Immediate Educational Feedback: Instantly celebrates right answers or gently guides wrong answers, explaining why the item belongs (or doesn't belong) in that bin.

I cannot push files directly to your GitHub repository from here because I do not have terminal or GitHub access. However, you can link and host the game on your repository in two quick ways:

Option 1: Using Git (Command Line)

  1. Save the game code above as index.html inside a folder on your computer.

  2. Open your terminal / Command Prompt in that folder and run:

    code Bash
    git init
git add index.html
git commit -m "Add EcoPark 3D educational trash sorting game"
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/sulphrtrioxide/Hands-on-Interactive-Web-Project.git
git push -u origin main

    (If the repository already has files in it, run git pull origin main --rebase before git push -u origin main.)

Option 2: Upload Directly on GitHub (No Terminal Needed)

  1. Save the game code above as index.html.

  2. Go to https://github.com/sulphrtrioxide/Hands-on-Interactive-Web-Project.

  3. Click Add file → Upload files.

  4. Drag and drop index.html and click Commit changes.

Turn It Into a Live Link (GitHub Pages)

Once index.html is in the repository, you can make it playable on any browser or embeddable on any website:

  1. On your GitHub repository page, go to Settings → Pages (in the left sidebar).

  2. Under Build and deployment → Source, select Deploy from a branch.

  3. Choose main branch and / (root) folder, then click Save.

  4. After 1–2 minutes, your game will be live at:

    code Text
    https://sulphrtrioxide.github.io/Hands-on-Interactive-Web-Project/

Identifying the Critical Error

I've discovered a critical error in the initialization sequence. I realize that the code neglects to initialize scene.background and scene.fog before calling buildMap("park"). This oversight leads to null references and immediately crashes the script due to the attempted calls to .setHex() on a null value. I'm now cross-checking all initialization calls for potential similar oversights. I'm also reviewing how buildAnimalCharacter handles color conversions, confirming that CSS hex strings are correctly interpreted in the current Three.js version.

Analyzing Pointer Events

I'm now focusing on mobile interaction handling, specifically pointerup and pointercancel events. I see that clientX and clientY are valid on pointerup, allowing correct checkBinHover calls, but on pointercancel, I need to prevent incorrect calls to handleDrop. I've also examined the HUD button click and drag use case with the endPointer function. Additionally, I'm now cross-referencing this to buildMap and assessing whether the trash item coordinates are within any of the map's circular regions such as the pond and ice pond.

Evaluating Coordinate Logic

I've confirmed that the calculated distance to (-10, -6) is 1.41, which places an animal on the ice pond, which is a neat interaction! I'm now implementing backdrop click-to-close functionality for the avatarModal, mapsModal, and guideModal elements for improved user experience. Regarding scoring, I've decided to reset the score to zero on "Play Again" but keep it when switching maps, enabling cumulative scores across worlds. I'm also ensuring the hint banner sits cleanly below the HUD on mobile and fades out after 6 seconds or on interaction. Finally, I'm examining the resize listener and renderer dimensions.

11.3s

I found and fixed the bugs in the previous code—most importantly, scene.background and scene.fog were not initialized before buildMap("park") called .setHex() on them, which caused a startup TypeError crash.

Fixes Made:

  1. Fixed Startup Crash: Initialized scene.background = new THREE.Color(...) and scene.fog = new THREE.Fog(...) before buildMap() runs.

  2. Added Three.js Load Check: Prevents a crash and shows a friendly message if the 3D library fails to load offline.

  3. Fixed pointercancel Handling: Cancelled touch gestures now cleanly reset the dragged item instead of accidentally dropping it.

  4. Memory Leak Fix: Added geometry/material cleanup in clearGroup() when switching animals or maps.

  5. Older Browser CSS Fallback: Added 100vh fallback before 100dvh for older iOS/Android browsers.

.bin-target[data-category="anorganic"] { --bin-bg: var(--anorganic); --bin-shadow: var(--anorganic-dark); } .bin-target[data-category="paper"] { --bin-bg: var(--paper); --bin-shadow: To add a Fullscreen toggle button (⛶) that works on desktops, tablets, Android, and embedded iframes, add these two small pieces to your index.html:

1. Add the Fullscreen Button to the Top HUD

Find the <nav class="hud-group" aria-label="Game Controls"> section and add the #btn-fullscreen button right after #btn-sound:

code Html
<button class="btn-3d btn-soft icon-btn-3d" id="btn-sound" title="Toggle Sound" aria-label="Toggle Sound">🔊</button>
<button class="btn-3d btn-soft icon-btn-3d" id="btn-fullscreen" title="Toggle Fullscreen" aria-label="Toggle Fullscreen">⛶</button>

2. Add the Fullscreen JavaScript Logic

Inside your <script>, right after the btn-sound click listener, add this block:

code JavaScript
// ==========================================
// FULLSCREEN FEATURE
// ==========================================
const btnFullscreen = document.getElementById("btn-fullscreen");

function isFullscreen() {
  return !!(document.fullscreenElement || document.webkitFullscreenElement || document.msFullscreenElement);
}

function updateFullscreenUI() {
  const active = isFullscreen();
  btnFullscreen.textContent = active ? "🗗" : "⛶";
  btnFullscreen.title = active ? "Exit Fullscreen" : "Enter Fullscreen";
  // Resize 3D canvas & confetti after entering/exiting fullscreen
  setTimeout(() => {
    camera.aspect = window.innerWidth / window.innerHeight;
    camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
    renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight);
    resizeConfetti();
  }, 100);
}

btnFullscreen.addEventListener("click", () => {
  playClickSound();
  const target = document.getElementById("game-container");

  if (!isFullscreen()) {
    const req = target.requestFullscreen || target.webkitRequestFullscreen || target.msRequestFullscreen;
    if (req) {
      Promise.resolve(req.call(target)).catch(() => {
        hintBanner.textContent = "📱 Fullscreen is not supported in this browser or iframe.";
        hintBanner.style.opacity = "1";
        setTimeout(() => { hintBanner.style.opacity = "0"; }, 3000);
      });
    } else {
      hintBanner.textContent = "📱 Fullscreen is not supported on this device.";
      hintBanner.style.opacity = "1";
      setTimeout(() => { hintBanner.style.opacity = "0"; }, 3000);
    }
  } else {
    const exit = document.exitFullscreen || document.webkitExitFullscreen || document.msExitFullscreen;
    if (exit) Promise.resolve(exit.call(document)).catch(() => {});
  }
});

document.addEventListener("fullscreenchange", updateFullscreenUI);
document.addEventListener("webkitfullscreenchange", updateFullscreenUI);

(Note: If you embed the game on another website using an <iframe>, keep allowfullscreen on the <iframe> tag so the fullscreen button works inside the embed too.)
